text: The lottery jackpot. The clerk at the prize office checked your numbers three times—five million, it's real.
Waiting at a red light on the corner, a talent scout stopped you: 'Ever thought about modeling for a magazine?' You assumed it was a scam—but the contract was real.
You were struck by lightning in a thunderstorm and lived. The doctor says the odds are one in ten million; you say there's been a key-shaped scar on your chest ever since.
Your family welcomed twin baby siblings. Half your childhood has smelled of baby formula ever since.
Cleaning out the attic, you unearthed a dust-covered old painting—authenticated as genuine. Some ancestor of yours had painted in secret.
The direct-admission notice arrived. A life without the gaokao made everyone in your class look at you differently.
The old man playing chess in the park suddenly took you on as an apprentice—only later did you learn he was a retired master craftsman. One craft for one livelihood.
That terminal diagnosis from three months ago was the hospital mixing up your scans. In those three months you learned to swim, made your apologies, quit your job—now what?
The fifty-yuan old bowl from a street stall turned out to be a prized piece of folk-kiln ware. You've trusted your gut ever since—and told this story to everyone you meet.
A video you shot on a whim passed a hundred million views. Brands lined up to sign you—and all you did that day was casually lift your phone.
You casually helped an old man who had fallen. A week later, a job offer arrived from the company run by his son—some coincidences in this world are real.
You appeared on a children's talent show. The whole country remembered the kid who played the piano wrong but bowed perfectly.
